rows.note: This is the all-purpose Cantonese noun for depression as a mental illness and is also commonly used for a depressive episode.

example.english: I think I have depression and have been seeing a doctor for several months.
example.traditional: 我覺得自己有抑鬱症，已經睇咗幾個月醫生。
example.jyutping: ngo5 gok3 dak1 zi6 gei2 jau5 jik1 wat1 zing3 ji5 ging1 tai2 zo2 gei2 go3 jyut6 ji1 saang1

rows.note: Use this for a prolonged period of severe economic contraction rather than an individual's low mood.

example.english: This economic depression caused global unemployment to soar.
example.traditional: 呢次經濟大蕭條令全球失業率急升。
example.jyutping: nei1 ci3 ging1 zai3 daai6 siu1 tiu4 ling6 cyun4 kau4 sat1 jip6 leot6 gap1 sing1

rows.note: Use this specifically for a meteorological low-pressure area.

example.english: The Observatory says a depression is approaching, so it may rain heavily tomorrow.
example.traditional: 天文台話有低氣壓靠近，聽日可能落大雨。
example.jyutping: tin1 man4 toi4 waa6 jau5 dai1 hei3 aat3 kaau3 gan6 ting1 jat6 ho2 nang4 lok6 daai6 jyu5

rows.note: Use this for a hollow or area of land lower than its surroundings.

example.english: This map marks the depression in the valley.
example.traditional: 呢幅地圖標出咗山谷入面嘅凹地。
example.jyutping: nei1 fuk1 dei6 tou4 biu1 ceot1 zo2 saan1 guk1 jap6 min6 ge3 aau1 dei6
